name: Janus Cosmos
primary_data_strategy: Hubble/MAST and Galaxy Zoo: Hubble public data; JWST/MAST confirmation stage
what_we_expect_to_find: tidal tails, arcs, shells and rings
jets and cavities associated with active galaxies
rare morphology that is under-characterized but astrophysical
why_these_are_expected: Public Hubble archives contain enormous numbers of galaxies and known anomaly searches already recover many interacting/merging systems and lensing structures.
interesting_candidate_definition: A structure that survives fixed multiscale planner proposals, matched spatial nulls, cross-band comparison, and independent re-evaluation.
replication_rule: A single visually striking cosmic image is never sufficient.

current_result.claim_ceiling: No anomaly, new physics, extraterrestrial intelligence, or hidden message is established by the scaffold or preflight.

data_provenance.galaxy_zoo_hubble: 113705 galaxies in the main GZH classification table
data_provenance.known_2026_context: NASA reported an AI-assisted Hubble archive search that found >1300 odd-looking objects, >800 not previously documented in scientific literature.

next_gate: Ingest source-confirmed HST multi-filter image cutouts, run FractalGPT blind proposals, then freeze candidate IDs before any semantic inspection.
